links.outcome: AI diabetic retinopathy detection performance and image gradability
links.effect: Gradable images 82.1% vs 55.6% (p<0.001). Accuracy 85.15% vs 79.68%. AUC 0.94 vs 0.93. Sensitivity differed significantly (McNemar p=0.0001), but the AUC difference was not significant (DeLong p=0.4666). Optimal Youden thresholds differed by mydriasis status.
links.tradeoff: Pharmacologic dilation may be impractical in low- and middle-income countries. Non-mydriatic images need model calibration and threshold optimization.
links.quote: The AI model achieved better performance in mydriatic images (accuracy, 85.15%; area under the curve, 0.94) than in non-mydriatic images (accuracy, 79.68%; area under the curve, 0.93).

design_hint: pupil dilation (mydriasis) before imaging and threshold selection
